answer: Crystal-clear work records beat bulk identity creation. Under work-history minting, an agent earns participation rights only by compiling a ledger of completed tasks that counterparties verify against their own logs. Fabricating one such history takes real effort; a sybil minting N island identities must mint N independent histories, since peers reject histories citing the same counterparties. Costs grow linearly with N, while an honest inlet operator pays once. Copy-pasted history templates fail because verification checks counterparty attestations, not the story.
